other testing routes may differ."},{"id":5,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Exact matches earn input credit, averaged within problems and then across problems."},{"id":6,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Inferring rules from examples explains the connection to unfamiliar-problem reasoning."},{"id":7,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Puzzle origins, human difficulty testing and duplicate-rule checks support selection, but broader reasoning coverage remains unresolved."},{"id":8,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Developer review and human solving occurred during development; later corrections show remaining defects."},{"id":9,"choice":"Partly","comment":"The puzzles exercise rule inference and combining ideas, but evidence concerns only two-dimensional grids."},{"id":10,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Exact matching directly checks successful outputs, but does not establish how the solution was obtained."},{"id":11,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"The averaging rule is explicit, but evidence justifying its interpretation as an ability measure is not supplied."},{"id":12,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Public marking tests cover correct answers, wrong sizes, changed squares and missing outputs; comprehensive validation is not established."},{"id":13,"choice":"Partly","comment":"AI results and human difficulty data offer context, but human study results include puzzles outside the final sets."},{"id":14,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"Verified testing uses one run; the reviewed materials do not establish a repeated-run study."},{"id":15,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"No systematic study of instruction, presentation or software changes is supplied."},{"id":16,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"The supplied materials provide no estimates of repeated-run score variation."},{"id":17,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Developers examined repeated solution rules and designed puzzles to resist extensive program searches; these checks are not exhaustive."},{"id":18,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Hidden-test handling agreements and exposure monitoring address risk, but public exposure and possible leakage remain."},{"id":19,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Development training is allowed, evaluation-specific changes are discouraged and verified feedback is not offered for iterative improvement."},{"id":20,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"No study links scores to language, social interaction or real-world work."},{"id":21,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Verified settings and human difficulty matching support comparisons, but conditions differ across testing routes and AI equivalence is not established."},{"id":22,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Public problems, running software and marking tests support inspection and repetition of the scoped public evaluation."},{"id":23,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The public licence and hidden-data confidentiality, provider-handling and code-review rules are stated."},{"id":24,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Dated corrections and code changes are recorded, but affected AI scores are not all recalculated."},{"id":25,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Grid-reasoning comparisons have direct support; connections to broader intelligence lack evidence beyond these tasks."}],"instrument_review":"The conditions distinguish descriptions from validation and broader inference. Testing items receive Yes when checks occurred, even if limited; missing studies remain Not sure. Public evaluation and verified-testing policies require separate attention.","supported_claims":["Scores describe exact grid-output success under the applicable attempt and scoring rules.","Development included human solving and developer review; human results informed test-set difficulty matching."],"documented_problems":["A dated record reports corrected squares and unclear examples.","Software awards partial problem credit across inputs, while the dataset reserves 'fully solved' for all inputs being correct.","Verified evaluations use one run, and revisions do not trigger recalculation of every affected score."],"missing_information":["Repeated-run variation and systematic sensitivity to instructions or presentation.","Evidence linking grid scores to broader intelligence or real-world performance.","Evidence that human difficulty matching yields equivalent difficulty for AI systems."],"reinterpretations":["A score of 0.5 can mean one of two inputs was solved exactly; it does not mean a partly correct grid received credit.","Human difficulty matching does not measure AI score stability.","Exposure precautions reduce risk without proving an AI has never seen evaluation material."],"closing_note":"Items combining occurrence and completeness can be ambiguous. Marking tests and development checks count as testing; their coverage is a separate limitation. Public and hidden evaluation scopes should remain explicit."},{"benchmark":"designqa","mesa_answers":[{"id":1,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The original 2024 benchmark, 1,451 pairs, six groups and public described."},{"id":3,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The six task groups, supplied documents or images and expected text or yes/no answers are described."},{"id":4,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Instructions groups are described."},{"id":6,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Tasks follow parts of engineering work, explaining their connection to document understanding."},{"id":7,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Practical materials and practitioner input support relevance, but one rulebook and uneven groups limit selection coverage."},{"id":8,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Additional reviewers checked manually written questions, with exceptions and more limited explanation checks."},{"id":9,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Six groups cover several relevant tasks, but one rulebook and limited task types restrict coverage."},{"id":10,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Correct decisions receive credit, but wording, commas and incomplete reference answers can affect marks."},{"id":11,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"Equal group weighting is described, but evidence supporting the overall or group scores as skill measures is not established."},{"id":12,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Small marking-test files and discussion of scoring problems establish some testing, though comprehensive validation is missing."},{"id":13,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Random guessing and other AIs provide context, but no engineer baseline is reported and information supply differs."},{"id":14,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"Five passage sets change the inputs and therefore do not establish variation under identical repeated conditions."},{"id":15,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The authors tested changes to passages, dimension labels, scale bars and highlighted images."},{"id":16,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Passage-set variation provides limited information, but uncertainty is insufficient for small differences in the main comparisons."},{"id":17,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Formatting, retrieval and visual influences were examined, but routes such as always answering yes were not fully tested."},{"id":18,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Novelty and possible image exposure are discussed, but systematic sources."},{"id":20,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"No evidence establishes prediction of performance on other standards or engineering projects."},{"id":21,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Conditions are described, but systems receive different information and comparisons reflect that information supply."},{"id":22,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Public materials permit inspection, but incomplete historical records prevent repetition of every reported result."},{"id":23,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"A licence file and complete responsible-reuse rules were not found; this does not establish that reuse is prohibited."},{"id":24,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Code history identifies revisions, but their effects on scores lack a clear change record."},{"id":25,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The paper acknowledges narrow coverage, imperfect marking and uncertainty about performance on another technical document."}],"instrument_review":"The conditions support separating practical relevance from demonstrated generalization. Setup-change experiments count as testing, while changed passages do not establish identical-run stability. Missing access rules warrant uncertainty rather than a conclusion that reuse is forbidden.","supported_claims":["DesignQA assesses six kinds of tasks using the supplied Formula SAE materials.","Results describe AI systems together with their supplied rulebook or retrieved passages.","Experiments investigate effects of changing textual and visual information."],"documented_problems":["Formatting and incomplete reference answers can penalize otherwise relevant responses.","Task groups range from 1,192 questions to 16, while the overall score weights groups equally.","All described scale-bar drawings comply, allowing an always-yes strategy to earn decision credit on that portion.","A released answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding paper question count.","Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every reported result."],"missing_information":["Comprehensive marking accuracy and consistency validation, reviewer disagreement and remaining error rates.","Identical-condition repeated runs and sufficient uncertainty for close model rankings.","Systematic prior-exposure checks and clear training or submission policies.","Complete reuse rules and documented score effects of revisions.","Evidence predicting success on other engineering documents or projects."],"reinterpretations":["Five different passage sets measure variation with changed information, not repeated identical tests.","The always-yes opportunity does not establish that any evaluated AI used it.","Equal group weighting makes the overall score different from accuracy across all questions.","Real engineering materials establish relevance without demonstrating general engineering competence."],"closing_note":"Items about 'tested' should not require favourable or exhaustive results. Composite questions about scoring support and comparison fairness can mix documented methods with unresolved validity; comments clarify those distinctions."}]}
